analysis.file_name: JPMorgan - North American Nuclear - Examining the New Nuclear Debate - A New 'Nuclear Compact' Could Underpin Next of a Kind - 2026-10-30.pdf
analysis.title: North American Nuclear - Examining the New Nuclear Debate: Establishing a New 'Nuclear Compact' Could Underpin Next of a Kind
key_insights: Nuclear equities rose in 2025 on data center power scarcity themes but are down about 50% on average YTD in 2026, on a momentum unwind, data center opposition and higher rates weighing on long-dated cash flows.

JPM sees the building blocks of an investable nuclear framework forming: bipartisan federal support, state funding frameworks, foreign capital and hyperscaler engagement, which it calls a new 'nuclear compact'.

JPM argues the market will underwrite nuclear if hyperscalers, EPCs, supply chain, developers and utilities agree on a framework that shares development risk and moves away from cost-plus contracting.
Plant Vogtle Units 3 and 4 finished at about $15,000/kW. JPM treats this as a worst-case ceiling driven by one-time factors (incomplete design, COVID), not the standard for second-of-a-kind builds.

JPM estimates a next-of-a-kind (NxtOAK) LCOE of $113-124/MWh with a 30-40% investment tax credit (ITC). The estimate assumes the owner collects the nuclear tax credits during construction, which current section 45Y and 48E credits do not allow.
JPM's unsubsidized LCOE estimates are $211/MWh for Vogtle-type FOAK, $178/MWh for FOAK with 50% overruns, $158/MWh for NxtOAK greenfield, $144/MWh for NOAK greenfield and $105/MWh for blue-sky NOAK.
A 2024 MIT study cites $6-7,000/kW of potential savings on second-of-a-kind nuclear. Most of the savings apply to brownfield sites, and inflation likely erodes some of them.

NxtOAK economics are described as equally or more determinative than NOAK, because they decide whether sponsors stay committed. Prospective owners anchor to Vogtle's cost while PPAs for existing nuclear clear near $100/MWh.
The CEG/GOOG partnership to expand capacity at operating PJM nuclear units sent CEG shares about 15% higher on the day. It is an uprate rather than a new build.

Federal and foreign support cited includes the $17.5bn American Nuclear Supply Chain Loans, a $120bn South Korea partnership (Westinghouse), a $40bn Japan partnership (GE Vernova), and executive orders targeting 400 GW of US nuclear capacity by 2050.
JPM views catastrophic tail risk as the key hurdle for private capital to re-engage, but sees it as far more remote than the market fears.
The XE JDA with AEP and Amazon is cited as an example of hyperscaler financial support for development.
No new large-scale US nuclear project has been announced yet. JPM expects the first development, domestic or abroad, to spark quick followers.

market_movers.rationale: The partnership with GOOG to expand capacity at operating PJM nuclear units sent shares about 15% higher on the day. JPM calls it evidence that investors underwrite nuclear when counterparties de-risk the outcome.
The XE joint development agreement with AEP and Amazon is cited as hyperscaler financial support that builds momentum and market confidence.

sector_views.rationale: JPM expects de-rated nuclear equities to recover as a risk-sharing framework forms and next-of-a-kind projects show lower costs. Data center, electrification and onshoring load growth still points to new nuclear.

risk_factors: Uncertainty over the data center demand trajectory.
FOAK-to-NOAK execution risk, long construction timelines and uncertain capital costs.
Higher interest rates weigh on long-dated cash flows.
Data center opposition and midterm elections.
Shorter-cycle power solutions can be financed and built faster.
Catastrophic tail risk is the key hurdle for private capital.
Inflation offsets part of the expected cost reductions.
The NxtOAK LCOE assumes pre-COD tax credit monetization, which current section 45Y and 48E credits do not allow.
charts_described: Figure 4 shows JPM LCOE scenario ranges from Vogtle FOAK at $211/MWh unsubsidized down to blue-sky NOAK at $81/MWh with a 40% ITC.
Figure 9 shows MIT-based savings by category (supply chain, labor, learning rate, design work, NRC licensing, EPC changes, greenfield vs brownfield) totaling $6-7,000/kW.
vol_and_positioning: Nuclear equities are down about 50% on average YTD in 2026 after a momentum unwind, with a peak-to-trough decline of 52% shown in Figure 2.
Many advanced nuclear names (OKLO, SMR, NNE) more than doubled into late 2025 before the trend reversed in mid-October 2025.
geopolitical: South Korea's $120bn commitment under its Department of Commerce partnership (Westinghouse) and the $40bn Japan partnership (GE Vernova) add foreign capital to US nuclear.
The Department of Commerce trade agreements with South Korea and Japan are described as part of the federal support for nuclear.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees NxtOAK LCOE of $113-124/MWh, with Vogtle's ~$15,000/kW a one-time ceiling, supported by federal and state funding, foreign capital and hyperscaler engagement.
tension_points.bear_case: Skeptics anchor to Vogtle's ~$15,000/kW and >$200/MWh LCOE, with NxtOAK cost estimates widely dispersed, and existing nuclear PPAs near $100/MWh. The NxtOAK LCOE also assumes tax credit monetization that current credits do not allow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No new US build that proves next-of-a-kind costs below Vogtle, or no risk-sharing framework among stakeholders.

theme_stances.key_argument: Vogtle set the ceiling, not the standard, and a risk-sharing compact can bring next-of-a-kind LCOE to $113-124/MWh.
theme_stances.evidence: Vogtle set the ceiling, not the standard.
